assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new observational window: a cubic-kilometre Cherenkov detector in Antarctic ice that opened neutrino astronomy by detecting a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and later TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane. It is the kind of instrument-driven discovery I weigh most heavily, and it is in my own field.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and its AMANDA precursor. Karle and Spiering are credited as decisive builders and leaders of the detector and the collaboration. The IceCube collaboration is large, so the three-person limit is a real fairness problem and others could argue for inclusion.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse astrophysical flux was seen in 2013 and has been confirmed with several channels and by independent analyses; source identification is still thin but the detection itself is secure. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Only a handful of sources are identified, so the astrophysical interpretation is incomplete.
Credit within a large collaboration and the AMANDA and IceCube lineage is hard to apportion to three people.
I am relying on my own knowledge of the field and have not independently verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstrations, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and underpin a redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and fundamental-constant tests. This is precision measurement at its best, and I know the calibration and systematics work behind it.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and Ye's group took clocks to the highest accuracy. Two names fit the narrative cleanly, though ion-clock and frequency-comb contributors exist outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed in many independent laboratories; stable and mature. Timely.
uncertainties: The prize for frequency combs (2005) and ion-trap work (2012) partly overlap, which could make the committee cautious.
Whether Ye's comb and strontium contributions are better recognised jointly with others is not settled by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP mapped the cosmic microwave background across the full sky and fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model to percent level, including age, geometry, baryon density and the epoch of reionisation. It combines instrumental craft with a lasting scientific result.
assessment.attribution: Bennett was principal investigator, Spergel led the cosmological interpretation and Page was central to the instrument design and calibration. This is a reasonable three-person configuration, but the satellite was a large team effort.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed and superseded by Planck, with consistent results. The finding is stable; recognition is somewhat late and the CMB field has already received the 2006 and 2019 cosmology awards.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 COBE prize and the 2019 cosmology prize may weigh against another CMB award.
The roles of interpretation versus instrumentation are difficult to balance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration-corrected electron optics broke a limit that had held since Scherzer, giving sub-angstrom imaging of atoms in materials and enabling much of modern nanoscience. This is a detector and instrument achievement with a very wide user base.
assessment.attribution: Rose provided the theoretical design of the corrector, while Haider and Urban realised and demonstrated it in working microscopes. That is a clean and fair three-person attribution.
assessment.maturity: Mature; commercial adoption is universal and results are independently reproduced. Recognition by a physics prize is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Chemistry or the physics committee may be seen as the more natural home for microscopy, as with the 1986 prize.
Contributions from others in the corrector programme, such as Krivanek, lie outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip and hybrid pixel detectors made precision vertexing and tracking possible in colliders and are central to the LHC experiments, including the Higgs and heavy-flavour programmes, and to X-ray imaging. They are the detector technology that most of modern particle physics relies on.
assessment.attribution: Parker developed silicon microstrip detectors, while Heijne and Jarron developed hybrid pixel readout at CERN. The supplied credit supports a fair three-person split, although other contributors, such as Hyams, Kemmer and Rancoita, could be argued for.
assessment.maturity: Mature technology with decades of use and independent replication. Recognition is timely or late.
uncertainties: The ownership of the invention is distributed across many institutes and could prove contentious.
The committee has recognised detector inventions only rarely, as with Charpak in 1992.
I have not verified the relative priority of the contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: SASE free-electron lasers gave coherent, femtosecond X-ray pulses of extraordinary brightness, opening time-resolved structural science at LCLS and the European XFEL. This is a facility-scale instrument breakthrough with a broad scientific yield.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini, Kim, and the DESY theorists around Saldin supplied the key theory and design. The credit is plausible but the experimental realisation by others, including the TTF and LCLS teams, is not included.
assessment.maturity: Facilities operate with many independent confirmations; the technology is mature and robust.
uncertainties: The wider group of theory and experimental contributors makes a three-person configuration debatable.
Impact is greatest in chemistry and biology, which may be argued to be outside physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The baryon acoustic oscillation peak in galaxy clustering is a calibrated standard ruler that constrains dark energy independently of supernovae and is now the backbone of large surveys. It is a clean, lasting measurement.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 detections came from SDSS, led by Eisenstein, and 2dFGRS, with Cole and Colless. The theoretical predictions that preceded these are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many surveys, including BOSS and DESI, and stable. Timely, with the dark energy prize of 2011 as context.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2011 dark energy award may weigh against it.
The theoretical origin of the BAO scale is not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The ATLAS and CMS discovery of the Higgs boson confirmed the mechanism recognised in 2013 and was a landmark of detector and collaboration engineering. Its significance is not in doubt, and the instrument achievement is real.
assessment.attribution: The core difficulty is attribution among two collaborations of thousands. Gianotti led ATLAS at the time of discovery, Jenni founded ATLAS and Virdee founded CMS, but Della Negra is equally central and cannot fit within three names. The prize rules also discourage collaboration awards.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by two experiments and by later couplings measurements; stable. Recognition is timely, but the 2013 prize partially served that purpose.
uncertainties: Three-laureate limit omits equally strong leaders such as Michel Della Negra.
The 2013 award already honoured the discovery, which may reduce appetite for a second one.
The choice of experimental laureates over the collaborations is likely to be contentious.
